newsitem.title: BULGARIA: RESTRUCTURING APPROVED FOR BULGARIA'S KREMIKOVTZI.
newsitem.headline: RESTRUCTURING APPROVED FOR BULGARIA'S KREMIKOVTZI.

text.p: Shareholders of Bulgaria's Kremikovtzi steelworks have approved a restructuring plan to pave the way for privatisation, officials said on Thursday.
A shareholders' meeting on Wednesday voted to transform the company to a joint stock company with a new board of directors, executive director Dimitar Milushev said.
Shareholders agreed to raise the company's capital to 200 billion levs from 18.5 billion levs.
Deputy Industry Minister Marin Marinov was elected chairman of the supervisory board and Milushev was re-elected as executive director and chairman of the board of directors.

Milushev said the industry ministry would be responsible for the restructuring of the plant. The government has drawn up a plan involving selling off smaller units and offering a 30 percent capital stake to investors.
Milushev said last month South Korea's Samsung Corp, Japan's Mitsubishi Corp and some Russian firms had shown potential interest in the plant, Bulgaria's biggest steelworks.
Some 3.71 percent of the steelworks were sold to employees or former employees through Bulgaria's mass voucher privatisation. The rest is owned by the state.
